oracle.description: templates/dispatch/tests/test_dispatch_release_artifacts_root.py decides correctness. Written from the spec row by an author with no access to any implementation; the single starts_red command runs the whole driver oracle set, so no other driver contract can regress unnoticed.

purpose: Make templates/dispatch/scripts/dispatch_release.py read its AUDITCTL_ARTIFACTS_ROOT default from the same place the cost hook now does. Today write_escalation calls os.environ.setdefault("AUDITCTL_ARTIFACTS_ROOT", "/projects/dev") under a comment claiming it matches templates/dispatch/hooks/log-session-cost.sh -- which is no longer true, because M-6a moved the hook onto the data file templates/dispatch/artifacts-root.default and the hook holds no literal any more. Add a function that resolves the default root from that data file, located RELATIVE TO THE DRIVER'S OWN FILE (there is already a HERE constant for this), never from the working directory and never from a hardcoded absolute path. Use it in write_escalation exactly where the literal was: setdefault semantics are unchanged, so an AUDITCTL_ARTIFACTS_ROOT already in the environment still wins and the default only fills in when it is absent. The literal string /projects/dev must no longer appear anywhere in dispatch_release.py. A missing or empty data file must not raise and must not stop an escalation from being written -- an escalation that cannot be recorded because a defaults file went missing is strictly worse than one recorded against a wrong root. Change nothing else in the file: STEPS, RETRY_STEPS, PR_STEP_NAMES, STOP_CONDITIONS, MAX_GATE_ATTEMPTS, the L-4 retry, the L-2 stop conditions, the PR step and the never-merge property all stay exactly as they are.
required_outcomes: the default root is resolved from templates/dispatch/artifacts-root.default, not from a literal
resolution is relative to the driver's own file, not to the working directory
an AUDITCTL_ARTIFACTS_ROOT already in the environment still wins
the literal /projects/dev no longer appears in dispatch_release.py
a missing or empty data file neither raises nor blocks the escalation record
every other driver contract is unchanged

acceptance_properties.fails_when: the resolver is absent or does not return the data file's stripped contents

acceptance_properties.requirement: resolution follows the driver, not the caller
acceptance_properties.fails_when: the resolver depends on the working directory or on a hardcoded absolute path
an already-set AUDITCTL_ARTIFACTS_ROOT is overwritten, or an absent one is not filled in

acceptance_properties.requirement: a missing defaults file never costs an escalation
acceptance_properties.fails_when: a missing or empty data file raises, or prevents the escalation record from being produced
any fixture in the L-1, L-2, L-4 or M-8 driver oracles fails

non_goals: the cost hook, which M-6a already moved onto the data file
hybrid_dispatch.py, the packet schema, the manifest or the dispatch policy
